questions.q: What does `transpile(qc, backend=backend, optimization_level=3)` actually produce?
options: The same circuit, unchanged, ready to submit
A circuit rewritten into the backend's native basis gates and mapped onto its physical qubit layout
A list of all backends compatible with the circuit
A simulated result of running the circuit
questions.explain: Transpilation rewrites the abstract circuit into the specific backend's native gate set and maps logical qubits onto physical ones respecting the coupling map — this transpiled circuit, not the original, is what gets executed.

questions.q: What does `optimization_level=3` trade off against lower levels like 0 or 1?
options: It runs faster to compile but produces a larger circuit
It produces the most aggressively reduced gate count/depth, at the cost of being the slowest to compile
It skips transpilation entirely
It only affects simulation, not real hardware
questions.explain: optimization_level 3 is the most aggressive setting for shrinking gate count and circuit depth, and it takes the longest to compile; level 0 is the opposite trade-off.

questions.q: Why does the transpiler insert SWAP gates during routing?
options: To slow down the circuit intentionally for safety
Because a two-qubit gate targets physical qubits that aren't adjacent on the backend's coupling map, so their states must be moved together first
To replace all single-qubit gates with two-qubit gates
Because the backend ran out of qubits
questions.explain: SWAP gates are inserted specifically when a two-qubit gate's target qubits are not connected on the backend's coupling map, physically relocating the relevant states so the real interaction can be applied.

questions.q: Per the standard textbook decomposition, how many CNOT gates does a single Toffoli (CCX) gate expand into when decomposed into a CX-plus-single-qubit-gate basis set?
options: 2 CNOT gates
3 CNOT gates
6 CNOT gates, plus several single-qubit H/T/T† gates
10 CNOT gates
questions.explain: This is a well-documented circuit identity: a single Toffoli standardly decomposes into 6 CNOT gates plus several single-qubit H, T, and T† gates — which is why circuits with multiple Toffolis can balloon in CNOT count after transpilation.

questions.q: Why is 'how many gates does my circuit have' only meaningfully answerable after transpilation for a specific backend?
options: Because `QuantumCircuit` objects don't store gates until transpiled
Because gate count depends only on the number of qubits, not the gates used
Because the actual gate count depends on the backend's native basis gates, its coupling map, and the chosen optimization_level — all backend-specific
Because transpilation always reduces every circuit to the same fixed size
questions.explain: The same abstract circuit can transpile into very different gate counts and depths on different backends, since basis gate rewriting and routing both depend on the specific target backend and the optimization_level used.
